qs.stem: Why is celecoxib associated with more cardiovascular events than its GI profile would suggest?

options.B: It raises renal blood flow excessively

options.D: PGI2 falls while platelet TXA2 is preserved

qs.why: Celecoxib blocks COX-2, lowering prostacyclin (PGI2) without a matching drop in platelet thromboxane (TXA2, made by spared COX-1) — the balance tips toward clotting.

qs.takeaway: Celecoxib: GI ↓ (COX-1 spared), CV ↑ (PGI2 ↓, TXA2 kept), kidney still affected.
qs.discriminator: Nonselective NSAIDs lower TXA2 too (bleeding risk); celecoxib does not.

whys.A: Reversed: celecoxib lowers GI risk and raises CV risk.

whys.D: Celecoxib is a COX-2 selective NSAID.
whys.E: Renal risk is similar to nonselective NSAIDs.

qs.takeaway: Celecoxib: GI ↓, CV ↑, kidney =.
qs.discriminator: There is no risk-free NSAID — only a different risk profile.
